setting: You are all members of a community allotment society in Melbourne, Australia, meeting on a shared site in the inner north. You know each other through society working bees, committee meetings and the seed swap, and you have all met in person many times. You know the basics of each other's jobs and households, but not much about each other's private lives beyond that.
opener: Ask whether anyone can cover the watering roster for the coming week.

Graham.knows: You know Mei as the society treasurer who keeps the accounts and works as a bookkeeper for a small builder, Kieran as the newest member, a PhD student in soil science, Denise as the seed-swap organiser and a primary school teacher, and Chloe as Denise's daughter, a barista who comes to working bees now and then.
Graham.texts: You message this group now and then, mostly when the society needs something organised or announced.

Mei.texts: You message this group now and then, mostly about money, invoices or payments for the society.

private_lines.Graham: You live in Coburg with your wife Helen. You're retired from teaching music, you conduct a community choir two evenings a week, and you spend most mornings pottering on your allotment or doing society paperwork at home.
private_lines.Mei: You live in Coburg with your partner and two primary-aged kids. You do bookkeeping for a small builder from a desk at home, most weekday afternoons are school pickups, and you get to the allotment on weekend mornings when you can.
private_lines.Kieran: You rent a room in a share house in Footscray. Most weekdays you're in the university lab or writing up your thesis at your desk, you often work late into the night, and you get to the allotment on weekend mornings to test your soil samples.
private_lines.Denise: You live with your daughter Chloe in Brunswick East. You teach at a local primary school on weekdays, you run the seed swap in the evenings and on weekends, and you spend your spare time on the allotment.
private_lines.Chloe: You live with your mum Denise in Brunswick East. You work shifts at a café on Sydney Road, usually early starts or closing shifts, and you spend your days off with friends or helping out on the allotment when your mum asks.
